In [[geometry]], the '''elongated pentagonal orthobicupola''' or '''cantellated pentagonal prism''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|38}}}}).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Elongated Pentagonal Orthobicupola |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-10-09 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref> As the name suggests, it can be constructed by elongating a [[pentagonal orthobicupola]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|30}}}}) by inserting a [[decagonal prism]] between its two congruent halves. Rotating one of the cupolae through 36 degrees before inserting the prism yields an [[elongated pentagonal gyrobicupola]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|39}}}}).

{{Johnson solid}}
[[File:J38 elongated pentagonal orthobicupola.stl|thumb|3D model of an elongated pentagonal orthobicupola]]

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[faces (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Elongated+pentagonal+orthobicupola Elongated pentagonal orthobicupola]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 25, 2010.</ref>

:<math>V=\frac{1}{6}\left(10+8\sqrt{5}+15\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{5}}\right)a^3\approx12.3423...a^3</math>

:<math>A=\left(20+\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}\left(10+\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{75+30\sqrt{5}}\right)}\right)a^2\approx27.7711...a^2</math>
